name: Big Stomp!

gist.Gigantisaur Chimera: The boss: enormous health, summoned by discarding three different Gigantisaurs from hand (which ends his turn). Each turn it hits one target harder for every different Gigantisaur in his discard pile.
gist.Gigantisaur King Trex: Enters by sacrificing another Gigantisaur; while it stands, every Gigantisaur in his hand can be summoned without levels.
gist.Gigantisaur Stomp: Free extra hit from any hero that has a truly huge creature beside it; one per hero per turn.
gist.Gigantisaur Raptoren: Brings a second Gigantisaur along and draws a card per Gigantisaur he controls.
gist.Gigantisaur Triceras: Discards one card to draw three, every turn.
gist.Gigantisaur Pteranos: Discards Gigantisaurs from hand to draw twice as many, stocking the discard pile for the Chimera.
gist.Gigantisaur Stegon: When one of his Gigantisaurs is hit he may discard a card to bounce the same damage back.
gist.Gigantisaur Ankylos: Discards a card to stun one of your targets for a turn.
gist.Gigantisaur Brachion: Takes hits meant for its hero, for a discard each.
gist.Alex, Trainer of Heroes: When he gains an Ability he fetches another for a team-mate; this is how Summoning Magic reaches level three.
gist.Kit, the Shark Researcher: Each Ability she gains fetches a creature or costs you small hits or a card.
gist.Performance: Ability that copies the one beneath it and raises it a level, for a little self-damage.
gist.Smuggler's Pier: Area: either player may buy cards for gold on their turn.
gist.Giga Steroids: A second action this turn, usable only for an effect (a Stomp-turn enabler).
gist.The Great Wall of Deri: Shaves a little off every hit his creatures take.

plan: Baylee spends the first turns doing nothing visible: Alex, Kit, Training and Performance pile up Summoning Magic until one hero can call a Gigantisaur. Then the board fills with one giant per hero, Triceras, Pteranos and the Pier keep his hand full while feeding the discard pile, every hero beside a giant gets a free Stomp each turn, and the Chimera closes. Stegon makes hitting the dinosaurs painful, Brachion shields a hero. The deck is honest and slow: the heroes are exposed for several turns, each hero holds only one Gigantisaur, and every defensive trick costs a discard.

looks.early: Three heroes with growing Ability stacks and no dinosaur yet.
looks.mid: One Gigantisaur beside each hero, each bigger than a hero; Stomps every turn, a thick discard pile.
looks.late: The Chimera looming, King Trex next to it, Baylee holding one or two cards and saying nothing.

opening.tell: No Gigantisaur is out; Alex and Kit are still stacking Summoning Magic.
opening.why: These are the only turns his heroes stand without a wall, and a Fire Bomb on the Summoning Magic stack buys another one.

midgame.tell: A Stegon stands beside Alex and Baylee holds spare cards for it.
midgame.why: Damage thrown at the dinosaurs vanishes into huge health pools and comes back through Stegon; answer only the Ankylos stun or the Stomp that would kill and send the rest past the giants.

crisis.tell: The Chimera is out and three different Gigantisaurs lie in his discard pile.
crisis.why: One card deals with the Chimera better than any amount of damage: Dark Gear takes it, Snow Cannon silences it for a turn, The Yeeting removes it.

endgame.tell: He has one or two cards left, and every Brachion or Stegon trick needs a discard.
endgame.why: His protection runs on discards and his hand is empty; the heroes behind the dinosaurs are ordinary.

opening.board: Baylee attaches Summoning Magic to Alex, who passes a second copy to Kit; nothing else is on the table.
